a mine and ship and cargo went down. However, of the 2500 men on board no one was lost. The Captain himself said that the escape was miraculous."
Now a word about possibilities and obligations.
Anyone may be enrolled: -- the sinner (atheist or believer) for conversion; the saint for further conversion and progress in sanctity - in RELIGION, THE SCIENCE OF OUR RELATIONSHIP WITH GOD AND OUR NEIGHBOR. (and, if you will, of our dependent on Both)
Obligations are practical. Active members, appreciating the opportunities offered by membership are urged to pray for the missions and the missionaries and for all members of the Associa- tion; and to offer Holy Communion when they can for these inten- tions. Those who can afford to do so, are asked to contribute to the material support - usually 50c annually or $5. as a perpetual member - more if they wish and $2. or more a deceased member - - perpetuall membership or participation. Direct and immediate bene- fits include five hundred and about twenty-five holy Masses every day or 188,500 holy Masses annyally, saying nothing of the indirect participation in all the good works of the whole Order otherwise in- cluding thousands of Holy Masses dai
